plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental cherry tree that produces clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms before its leaves emerge. Its branches arch widely, creating a canopy of pale blooms that drift down as petals in the breeze.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry is the star of Japanese hanami festivals, and the 1912 gift of trees from Tokyo to Washington D.C. started the National Cherry Blossom Festival, which is timed around the peak bloom in late March.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler outer petals. It carpets woodlands and meadows in spring and is a classic herald of the season in cool temperate zones.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Spain; widely naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain the compound galantamine, which has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A spectacular Himalayan tree bearing huge, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches. The blossoms can reach up to 25 cm across and make a dramatic display in spring.
plants.location: Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, northeastern India, southwest China); cultivated in mild gardens in the UK, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, evolving before bees existed, so their flowers are sturdy enough to be pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.commonName: Autumn Crocus (Southern Hemisphere bloom variants such as Nerine bowdenii)
plants.description: In the Southern Hemisphere, where March 22 falls in early autumn, bulbs such as nerines and colchicums burst into bloom on bare stems, bringing a surprising show of color as the weather cools.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (March to May)
plants.location: South Africa, Australia, New Zealand, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Colchicum bulbs are the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.
